restrictions: Complete fixed-IV SHA3-256 sponge (rate 1088, capacity 512, suffix 0x06, pad10*1), prefix rounds 0 through 5, all 256 output bits; every message is exactly 64 bytes (one block).

Generic birthday search over N = 255*2^120 messages in 255*2^88 groups of 2^32. Group g has a fresh structured 64-byte prefix P_g: 256 uniform bits in lanes 1, 2, 5, 6; lanes 0 and 7 are 0; with c1 = L1 XOR L6 XOR 2^63, lane 3 = 0x06 XOR rotr(c1, 1) and lane 4 = NOT rotl(c1, 1) (the prefix map is injective). Message m(g, z) is P_g with LE32(z) XORed into bytes 8..11 and 48..51 (low halves of lanes 1 and 6, one theta column). This makes round 1 linear in z (the linear structures of Guo, Liu and Song, ASIACRYPT 2016, brought to this track by Th0rgal's 4867f093 with lanes 0 and 5; lanes 1 and 6 are our variant). Groups are processed in batches of 256 (one group per bit position of every 256-bit word, bitsliced), z = gray(t) for t = 0..2^32-1, slots offered in the fixed order decode_slot(q) = 32*(q mod 8) + floor(q/8), q = 0..255. Message (beta, t, q) has number n = beta*2^40 + t*2^8 + q.

Each z-step of a batch (256 messages) is an exact counted, fully unrolled word-RAM program (branches only in the ctz tree, the table step with its candidate path, and the loop test; 32 fused straight-line leaves) of at most 31,410 executed primitives on its worst path (leaves 31,380..31,410): an AND-free incremental round 2 (z-bit j flips a fixed 22-word set of A2 by all-ones; only read words are flipped; 508 round-3 input words get fixed XOR patches merged into the round-3 loads; at most 1,816 ops), lane-complement rounds 3-5 with theta at the store and start planes (2, 39, 34), the round 4-5 dependency cones (1,363 and 175 words), the last round on 35 bit planes (140-bit key), a rotating-frame zero-row transpose (3,418 ALU ops), a 6-op tagged-id table step per message, and loop control. Charge: 31,410/256 + setup (< 2^-20) per message; batch setup is a counted 52,558-op program.

Classical probabilistic 256-bit word RAM under collision-frontier-v5 with 64 registers as our stated assumption (the program uses all 64: at most 62 per compiled leaf, register-allocated by interval colouring after SSA and store-to-load forwarding, plus the step counter and the table word c). One six-round permutation costs 1 unit; every executed load, store (direct or register-addressed), logic operation, shift or rotation, add, comparison, conditional branch, immediate move and random word costs 1/1626; constant addresses and immediates are instruction fields. The 64-register reading does not cover a register bank of thousands of words; no bound is claimed under such a reading (it would give 123.815 here; not claimed) or a memory-to-memory reading. Charging also one address addition per direct access and one move per ALU immediate gives 40,480 per z-step and 124.636; also each shift or rotation amount 41,266 and 124.664.

Table: S has 2^140 words at address 0 and is never initialised; the key K < 2^140 is the address; the slot holds TAG*2^128 + n (TAG a uniform 128-bit word drawn once per run). Hot path per message: load, XOR with c = TAG*2^128 + n, compare < 2^128, branch, store c, c += 1. A slot whose high half equals TAG is a candidate: both messages are rebuilt from their numbers and stored prefixes and evaluated in full (2 units); the run halts only on equal 256-bit digests of distinct messages, otherwise it counts the candidate and continues (at most 68 extra ops incl. the jump back; halting step at most 68 ops), aborting at the hard cap VCAP = floor(N^2/2^141) + floor(N^2/2^148) + 2^91 + 2^61. Garbage candidates (never-written words) have expectation <= N*2^-128 for any initial memory.

Time bound in every run (no restarts): T <= N*(31,410/256 + 2^-20)/1626 + VCAP*(2 + 68/1626) + (2 + 68/1626) + 1 < 2^124.27096, proved by an exact integer inequality (proof Section 8). The success probability 0.39 (model value 0.39106) relies on the declared heuristic H1 for F1, F2 and the genuine-candidate part of the abort probability (<= 2^-100); garbage candidates add <= 2^-61 by Markov and equal messages from two groups (F3) < 2^-33, both without heuristic. Output correctness and all resource bounds are unconditional.

No cryptanalytic weakness of SHA3 is claimed: this is a constant-factor improvement of a full-digest birthday search under the operation-level cost model. Memory is about 2^145 bytes (reported only, not a Pareto improvement).

heuristics.statement: For the failure events F1, F2 and the genuine-candidate part of F4 (proof Section 7), the N = 255*2^120 digests of the grouped message set {m(g, z)} (independent prefixes P_g, each uniform over the 2^256 structured prefixes of Section 2, all z in {0,1}^32, processed in any fixed order chosen independently of the digests, in particular the order of Section 2: batch by batch, t = 0..2^32-1 with z = gray(t), slots p = decode_slot(q) = 32*(q mod 8) + floor(q/8) for q = 0..255) behave like N independent uniform 256-bit values, i.e. Pr[F1] <= exp(-N(N-1)/2^257), Pr[F2] <= N^3/6 * 2^-396 and, since the 140-bit key is a fixed function of 140 digest bits, the number Y1 of message pairs with equal keys has E[Y1] <= N^2/2^141 and Var[Y1] <= E[Y1].
heuristics.scope: Only the success probability (Section 7) uses H1, through Pr[F1], Pr[F2] and Pr[Y1 >= E + floor(N^2/2^148) + 2^91] <= 2^-100 (Chebyshev). The garbage-candidate part of the abort (<= 2^-61, Markov on E[Y2] <= N*2^-128 with a uniform run TAG), F3 (< 2^-33, counting), evaluator exactness, verification of every output, and all time, memory and preprocessing bounds are unconditional (the candidate cap makes the time bound hold in every run). For every z, P -> m(P, z) permutes the structured-prefix set (XORing z into lanes 1 and 6 keeps c1), so m(g, z) is uniform over that set for every z; cross-group pairs (all but a 2^-96 fraction of pairs) therefore provably collide with probability >= 2^-256 each (Cauchy-Schwarz), and the expected number of colliding pairs is at least (1-2^-96) N(N-1)/2^257 without H1; H1 is needed for the second-moment behaviour behind Pr[F1], for F2 and for Y1. Bitslicing, batching, the incremental round 2, the start planes, the dependency cone, the compiler, the 140-bit key and the fixed encodings change neither the message set nor any digest value; they fix only the processing order, which depends on (batch, t, q) and never on digests.
heuristics.extrapolation: Tested at scale only: four organizer-executed scaled analogues with N_t = 2^9 messages and an 18-bit mask of kept digest bits (N_t^2/2^18 = 1, close to N^2/2^256 = (255/256)^2), all on structured prefixes and computing digests with an evaluator that mirrors the counted program (linear-structure incremental round 2 with the program's read-only flips, storage polarity and fixed patch expressions; lane-complement rounds with theta at the store and the start planes 2, 39, 34; rounds 4-5 computed in full, then every word outside the Lemma 10 cone replaced by an unrelated constant; last round on the 35 kept planes at the program's low-aligned key rows; the rotating-frame zero-row transpose, checked against the full transpose; processing order; every key also run through the tagged-id table with adversarial garbage): 256 groups x 2, 16 groups x 32, a single group of 512 and 4 groups x 128 with the varying z bits at 25..31. Every organizer trial checks the whole 140-bit key against an independent direct sponge (its first 4 and one at every step t = 2^i), the exact 22-word all-ones support of each z-bit used, and the maintained A2 and round-3 input against a rebuild from the prefixes. Participant-reported local replays (not organizer evidence): bs3-rv-1 96/97/95/96, committee-c1 101/108/112/109 of 256 (uniform model 100.6 +- 7.8). Participant-reported local statistics (proof Section 10.3), 12,288 trials per layout: z +0.09 / +0.41 / +2.38 / +0.42 (full-width / spread / single-group / high-z); 24,576 further single-group trials z -1.10, pooled single-group z +0.48; masked-pair variance/mean 0.991 / 1.008 / 0.987 (1.006 on the further runs) / 0.985, consistent with Var[Y1] <= E[Y1]. The claim extrapolates uniform-model behaviour to N = 255*2^120, the 256-bit digest and its 140-bit truncation.
heuristics.limitations: H1 is not proved. Within a group, round 1 is linear in z and A2 = A2(0) XOR sum_j z_j E_j with fixed group-independent vectors E_j (all-ones on 22 words; Lemmas 2-3), a stronger structure than in a generic search; five further nonlinear chi layers (rounds 2-6) follow, but masked low-width experiments cannot exclude a structural effect that appears only at full width. Within a group the digest has degree at most 2^5 = 32 in z; z has 32 bits, so no degree-based zero-sum exists on any affine subspace of z. The experiments use a full dictionary of masked keys, so the table loss F2 and the candidate count Y1 are bounded only under H1. Organizer seeds are public. The scaled experiments resolve the success frequency only to about +-0.03 at 256 trials. The 0.00106 allowance between the model value 0.39106 and the claimed 0.39 is not statistically certified. F4 is the most sensitive use of H1: by Cauchy-Schwarz any non-uniformity of the 140-bit key can only raise E[Y1], and the cap VCAP tolerates a relative excess of 2^-7 (0.78%) over N^2/2^141, while the scaled experiments resolve the masked-pair mean only to about 1% (pooled 1.008 +- 0.006 of the uniform model); within-group pairs would need an average key-collision probability above about 2^-51, or above about 2^-19 for the pairs of one z-difference, to matter.
